title: OpenAI Responses compatibility: mapping plan and parity gaps for streaming, function/tool calling, and structured outputs
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Analyze and implement a pragmatic compatibility layer that maps Redwood's Core API semantics to the OpenAI Responses API surface. Focus areas: streaming semantics, tool/function calling ergonomics, and structured output (JSON schema) parity. Produce a shim in the request gateway that preserves Redwood guarantees (latency SLOs, typed tool args, KV/cache behavior) while maximizing compatibility for customers migrating existing OpenAI Responses integrations.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway exposes a toggle 'openai_responses_mode' that enables request/response transformation to/from OpenAI Responses shapes
Streaming: server-sent events produced to clients mimic OpenAI delta stream format (role/content/delta and finalization events) for text + tool-invocation sequences
Function/tool calling: incoming OpenAI-style function_call requests are mapped to Redwood tool invocation model with parameter validation, and tool responses stream back using expected events
Structured outputs: Redwood’s structured output config supports OpenAI-style JSON schema validation and validation errors are surfaced in a compatible format
Automated integration tests cover: text streaming, function call round-trip, tool error propagation, and mismatched schema failure modes
Performance: compatibility transformation layer adds <6ms median request overhead for non-streamed requests and <8% p95 overhead for streamed requests in preliminary benchmarks
technical_decision: Implement a protocol translation layer in the API gateway rather than changing runtime kernels. The layer will: 1) accept OpenAI Responses shapes (messages, functions, function_call) and translate to Redwood internal request model; 2) wire runtime events to an OpenAI-compatible SSE event stream; 3) perform JSON schema validation using existing structured-output validators and convert validation errors to OpenAI-style 'tool' or 'content' error events. Trade-offs: keeps runtime stable and reduces risk to existing customers, at cost of additional gateway complexity and duplication of some validation logic. Long-term goal to converge API models when runtime versions allow.
tasks: Spec: finalize mapping table for messages => Redwood prompts, including role mapping and system/message precedence
Spec: define event stream envelope mapping (delta chunks, function_call.start/args/completion, done)
Gateway: implement request parser for OpenAI payloads and canonicalize to Redwood request body
Gateway: implement response streamer that emits OpenAI-compatible SSE sequence while preserving Redwood tokenization and truncation signals
Runtime: add a lightweight hook to emit tool-invocation intermediate events (tool stdout chunks) to gateway
Testing: e2e harness with example OpenAI client that expects standard Responses behavior (streamed function calls, final structured json)
Docs: migration guide with examples for common patterns (chat -> responses, function_call -> tool, json_schema mapping)
